findings.title: tout is a pronoun in this sentence
findings.detail: The object of ranger is tout, meaning everything. The core labels this ID as an adverb. The sentence and translations are natural, but the POS supplied to learners and exercise grouping does not describe this use.
findings.observedSentence: J'ai tout rangé dans le même tiroir.

findings.title: bien modifies va rather than a noun

findings.observedSentence: Depuis son retour, tout va bien.

findings.title: Chinese turns necessity into an observed attitude
findings.detail: The French says hygiene is essential in this kitchen. The Chinese says the kitchen places great importance on hygiene, asserting a practice or attitude rather than the necessity stated by the source.

findings.title: Chinese solo translation adds completed aspect
findings.detail: The French, English, Korean and other translations use a present or general action. 演奏了一段 adds a completed-event reading in the standalone Chinese sentence. Prefer an unmarked present/general formulation.

limits: This is an AI editorial sample review, not fluent-speaker or native-speaker review.
Only the listed 120 of 1,932 authored rows and their linked corrections were linguistically reviewed. Other examples and unlinked corrections are not approved by this report.
The deterministic sample is weighted towards the first and final rows; it does not estimate a population error rate.
Legacy rows without additional-language translations were checked only in FR/EN/KO; absent backfill was not treated as a mistranslation.
A no-actionable-finding result means no issue was identified in this pass, not certification of correctness.
All suggested changes are unapplied. French authored and correction source files were not modified.
Medical or legal definitions not specifically investigated here are not independently certified.
